editorial:
Imagine finally finishing high school and having the whole world open up in front of you. That is exactly where you find Lou, Malik, Fiona, Solal, Paul, and Théo. These six friends are done with exams and ready to leave everything behind for one big trip across Europe. The vibe is all about freedom, youth, and that feeling of being invincible. You get to follow them as they jump from city to city on trains, making mistakes and meeting strange people along the way. It feels like a digital scrapbook of a summer you never want to end, capturing that awkward but exciting transition from being a kid to becoming an adult.

What really works here is the chemistry between the group; they feel like real friends who actually know how to push each other's buttons. The pacing stays quick, and while some of the drama is a bit predictable, the scenery is beautiful. If you enjoy lighthearted stories about finding yourself, you will love this.
endingExplained: As the trip comes to a close, the friends realize that their bond has changed forever. They face some tough arguments and romantic tension, but they eventually forgive each other. The movie ends with them returning home, but they aren't the same kids who left. They have grown up and learned how to handle real-life problems. It wraps up on a hopeful note, showing that while the trip is over, their friendship will last into adulthood.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories and travel adventures.
